description: Left navigation shell. Input: the current route. Output: a nav rail rendering exactly three entries labelled Operational Picture, Hypotheses, Scenario Control, with the entry matching the current route marked active and exposed as the current page to assistive tech. Constraints: exactly three entries, no fourth; drill-down tables and system health are not entries. Failure case: rendering a fourth nav entry, or rendering zero active entries when the route matches a known screen, fails the spec. Refs: FR-701, FR-709, US-A1, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.7.

System-health status strip in the nav footer. Input: a system-health value from the operational-picture contract. Output: a compact strip in the navigation footer showing the health state as a categorical label. Constraints: it is a strip, not a screen and not a nav entry; state renders as a categorical label only. Failure case: rendering health as a percentage such as 98% uptime, or promoting health to a fourth nav entry, fails the spec. Refs: FR-702, FR-715, ui-001, nav-001.

Operational Picture status bar. Input: operationalPicture.scenario. Output: a top bar showing the scenario name badge and a persistent data-mode badge reading SYNTHETIC ENVIRONMENT DATA. Constraints: the data-mode badge is unconditional and cannot be dismissed or collapsed; it renders even when scenario data is absent. Failure case: the data-mode badge missing, or hidden behind a loading or empty state, fails the spec. Refs: FR-703, NFR-303, US-A7.

Active hypothesis cards in the right rail. Input: operationalPicture.hypotheses. Output: one card per active hypothesis showing title and confidence as a Low/Medium/High pip; activating a card navigates to that hypothesis on Hypothesis Detail. Constraints: confidence renders via the ui-001 primitive; an empty list renders an explicit no active hypotheses state rather than a blank rail. Failure case: an empty hypothesis list rendering an empty rail with no message, or a card rendering confidence as a number, fails the spec. Refs: FR-707, FR-715, ui-001, hyp-001, US-A4.

Detection summary panel. Input: operationalPicture.detectionSummary. Output: anomaly counts per category plus an overall severity rendered as Low/Medium/High. Constraints: counts are integers and may be shown as integers; severity is categorical only; no anomaly score, signal integrity, or confidence figure is rendered as a percentage or decimal. Failure case: rendering a severity of 0.82 or 82% fails the spec. Refs: FR-707, FR-715, ui-001, NFR-203.

Tabbed exception panel. Input: the operational-picture payload for the current view filter (op-007, api-007). Output: one panel with three tabs labelled RF (n anomalous), Tracks (n degraded), Events, listing the rows the current filter admits, with a footer reading +n nominal hidden and a View all link. Constraints: the default filter state is Anomalous only, so nominal rows are absent from the first render; the hidden count comes from the suppressed-count metadata on the response, not from counting the payload, because server-side filtering means the excluded rows never arrive; n in the tab label equals the number of rows shown. Failure case: a nominal RF sensor appearing while the filter is Anomalous only, or the footer count being derived from the payload and therefore reading zero whenever the backend filtered, fails the spec. Refs: FR-708, FR-716, FR-809, US-A1, op-007, api-007, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.7.

Drill-down tables. Input: activation of the View all link in an exception panel footer (op-004). Output: a full table over the same contract data, showing nominal and anomalous rows: full RF observation stream from the RF tab, full track inventory from the Tracks tab. Constraints: reachable only from panel footers, never from the nav; it is a view over the same data, not a new data source. Failure case: adding a nav entry for a drill-down table, or a drill-down fetching from an endpoint the panel does not use, fails the spec. Refs: FR-709, FR-701, nav-001, op-004.

Timeline strip. Input: operationalPicture.timelineEvents. Output: a horizontal strip rendering each event with its label and time, ordered oldest to newest. Constraints: ordering is by event time and independent of array order in the input; an empty list renders an explicit empty state. Failure case: events supplied out of order rendering out of order, or an empty list rendering a bare strip with no message, fails the spec. Refs: FR-710, hyp-001.

View filter control. Input: analyst selection of Anomalous only, Nominal only, or All. Output: the selection is sent to the backend as the view parameter (api-007), and the returned payload drives the map (map-003) and the exception panel (op-004) together, so the two always agree about what is shown. Constraints: default state is Anomalous only, preserving US-A1; the selection persists across polls rather than resetting on each refresh; drill-down tables stay unfiltered, since they are the show-everything view by definition. Failure case: the map showing all entities while the panel still shows only anomalous ones, or the filter resetting to the default on the next poll tick, fails the spec. Refs: FR-716, FR-809, US-A1, US-A9, op-004, map-003, api-007.

Playback transport control. Input: a scenario run's simulated-time window and analyst interaction with play, pause, speed, and scrub. Output: a playback cursor in simulated time driving the map render (map-004), with the current cursor position displayed. Constraints: the transport operates over simulated scenario time, never wall clock, consistent with anom-009; scrubbing to any point in the window is permitted, including backwards; pausing holds the cursor rather than resetting it. Failure case: playback speed altering the reported simulated time of a rendered position, so that the same cursor shows different data at 1x and 4x, fails the spec. Refs: FR-717, US-A10, anom-009, map-004, api-008, scn-004.

Confidence and severity rendering primitive, the global no-fake-precision invariant. Input: a confidence or severity value. Output: a rendered Low, Medium, or High label or pip. Constraints: the accepted input domain is exactly Low|Medium|High; the component never formats a number into a percentage or decimal; every screen renders confidence and severity through this primitive rather than inline. Failure case: passing 0.87 or 87 renders nothing and surfaces a development-time error rather than displaying 87%. Refs: FR-715, NFR-203, AC-11, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.5.

MapView adapter boundary. Input: aircraft tracks, RF sensors, and anomaly zones from the operational-picture contract. Output: a rendered map with a marker layer per entity kind. Constraints: MapView is the only module in the repo importing MapLibre GL JS or any map library, so it can be mocked wholesale in tests; no other component imports map types or calls map APIs. Failure case: a second module importing maplibre-gl fails the spec, and a repo-wide import check must assert this. Refs: FR-704, FR-705, US-E2, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 10.

MapView graceful placeholder. Input: absent or empty tile-source configuration. Output: a labelled placeholder region showing entity counts and a message that no tile source is configured. Constraints: no crash, no blank region, no thrown error, no network request attempted; the surrounding screen renders normally. Failure case: an unset tile-source env var producing a blank pane or an unhandled exception fails the spec. Refs: FR-705, NFR-102, map-001.

Anomalous items highlighted on the map. Input: tracks, sensors, and anomaly zones each carrying an anomalous or nominal state. Output: anomalous entities render visually distinct from nominal ones and carry a non-visual anomalous marker for tests and assistive tech; selecting one emits a selection event identifying the entity and any linked hypothesis. Constraints: distinctness is asserted through the entity state exposed in the accessible name, not through CSS classes; nominal entities are never highlighted. Failure case: an entity flagged anomalous in the contract rendering identically to a nominal one fails the spec. Refs: FR-706, US-A2, US-A3, map-001, hyp-001.

Track playback rendering. Input: buffered aircraft positions across a simulated-time window and the playback cursor from op-008. Output: aircraft rendered at their interpolated position for the cursor, each with a trailing path over a configured lookback, with anomalous track segments visually distinct from nominal ones and anomaly zones appearing and clearing as their windows enter and leave the cursor. Constraints: interpolation is client-side between buffered frames, so motion is smooth independently of the poll interval; all map work stays inside the MapView boundary per map-001. Failure case: a track whose buffer has not yet loaded must hold its last known position and be marked stale, not jump to a default coordinate or vanish. Refs: FR-717, FR-718, US-A10, map-001, map-003, op-008, api-008.

Health endpoint. Input: GET /api/v1/health. Output: 200 with a JSON body reporting service status. Constraints: no database dependency, so it answers before persistence exists; every route is mounted under the /api/v1 prefix by a single APIRouter, so the prefix is declared once and no handler hard-codes it; the route is tagged system for OpenAPI grouping; the backend owns the full path, so neither the nginx proxy nor the Vite dev proxy rewrites or strips /api. Failure case: returning 200 while the app has failed to start, requiring a database connection to answer, or serving the endpoint at an unversioned path such as /health, fails the spec. Refs: FR-801, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.8, docs/qa.md section 16.

Operational picture endpoint. Input: GET /api/v1/operational-picture. Output: 200 with a payload whose shape matches frontend/src/types/operationalPicture.ts exactly: scenario, hypotheses, detectionSummary, rfSensors, aircraftTracks, timelineEvents. Constraints: field names and nesting mirror the TypeScript contract; confidence and severity values are Low|Medium|High strings; a contract test asserts shape parity in both directions. Failure case: adding, renaming, or dropping a field on either side without the other changing fails the contract test. Refs: FR-802, FR-715, ui-001, api-003, docs/implementation.md Phase 5.

Frontend data access via polling. Input: a poll interval and the backend base URL. Output: a single API module fetching /api/v1/operational-picture on an interval and handing the typed contract to the screen. Constraints: exactly one module performs the fetch; no WebSocket, EventSource, or push transport exists anywhere in the repo; on fetch failure the app falls back to the mock and surfaces a degraded-data indicator rather than blanking. Failure case: a 500 or network error clearing the operational picture, or any push transport appearing in the dependency tree, fails the spec. Refs: FR-807, US-E4, NFR-102, api-002.

Hypothesis read endpoints. Input: GET /api/v1/hypotheses and GET /api/v1/hypotheses/{id}. Output: a list of hypothesis summaries, and a full hypothesis with evidence, uncertainty, alternatives, generator, and status. Constraints: the detail payload includes the producing generator so the UI can satisfy ai-010; confidence is a Low|Medium|High string. Failure case: GET /api/v1/hypotheses/{unknown-id} must return 404 with a JSON error body, not 200 with null and not a 500. Refs: FR-804, FR-713, hyp-001, ai-010.

Analyst feedback endpoint. Input: POST /api/v1/hypotheses/{id}/feedback with a verdict of confirm, reject, needs-more-evidence, or false-positive, and an optional note. Output: 200 with the updated hypothesis status persisted. Constraints: verdict is validated against the enum before any write; status transitions follow New, Under review, Confirmed, Rejected, Inconclusive. Failure case: an unrecognised verdict returns 422 and leaves hypothesis status and the feedback table unchanged; an unknown hypothesis ID returns 404. Refs: FR-601, FR-602, FR-604, FR-805, fbk-001, fbk-002.

Scenario control endpoints. Input: POST /api/v1/scenario/start with scenario type, parameters, seed, and batch count; POST /api/v1/scenario/reset; GET /api/v1/scenario/runs. Output: a run record with its ID and status; a cleared run state; a list of recent runs with type, parameters, seed, and outcome. Constraints: start echoes back the seed actually used so a run is always reproducible from its record, including when the caller omitted one. Failure case: starting with an unknown scenario type returns 422 and creates no run row; reset while no run is active succeeds idempotently rather than erroring. Refs: FR-806, FR-201, FR-204, scn-001, scn-004.

Server-side view filtering. Input: GET /api/v1/operational-picture with a view parameter of anomalous, nominal, or all. Output: a payload containing only the matching rfSensors, aircraftTracks, and timelineEvents, plus metadata carrying the suppressed count per collection. Constraints: filtering happens in the query, not by returning everything and discarding client-side, so the payload shrinks with the selection; the suppressed counts are what keep op-004's hidden footer truthful once rows stop arriving. Failure case: an unrecognised view value must return 422 rather than silently defaulting to all, and a filtered response omitting the suppressed-count metadata fails the spec. Refs: FR-809, FR-716, api-002, op-004, op-007.

Time-windowed track query for playback buffering. Input: a scenario run ID and a simulated-time span. Output: aircraft positions across that span, ordered by time per aircraft, sufficient for the frontend to interpolate between frames. Constraints: the frontend buffers ahead of the cursor and issues one request per span rather than one per frame, so the request rate is decoupled from the frame rate per FR-718; the span is bounded server-side to cap payload size. Failure case: a requested span exceeding the bound must be rejected or truncated with the truncation reported, never silently served in full; a span outside the run's recorded window must return an empty series, not an error. Refs: FR-810, FR-718, US-A10, op-008, map-004, adp-001.

Ground truth is never exposed outside the evaluation harness. Input: any API response, canonical observation, anomaly, evidence bundle, or hypothesis. Output: none of them carry the injected ground truth for the run. Constraints: the generator records what it injected on scenario_runs.ground_truth and that column is read by the evaluation harness only; no adapter, DAL record, detector input, API response, or evidence bundle may carry it, whether as a field, a label, or an inferable artefact such as a scenario-type string on an observation; GET /api/v1/scenario/runs may report that a run has ground truth recorded but never its content while the run is scorable. Failure case: an /api/v1/operational-picture or /api/v1/anomalies response including the scenario type or the injected event for the active run fails the spec, because a detector or an analyst able to see the answer invalidates every metric computed from that run. Refs: FR-207, FR-806, NFR-604, US-R5, AC-04, scn-002, adp-002, evb-001, eval-002.

Core schema and migrations. Input: an empty PostgreSQL database with the PostGIS extension. Output: tables observations, anomalies, evidence_bundles, hypotheses, analyst_feedback, and scenario_runs created by ordered migration files, with geometry columns on observations.location and anomalies.affected_area. Constraints: a documented migration convention; migrations apply cleanly from empty; source-specific fields live in the observation payload so the canonical table stays stable. Failure case: applying migrations twice from empty must not error, and a missing PostGIS extension must fail loudly at migration time rather than at first query. Refs: FR-901, FR-902, FR-906, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 9.

Hypothesis reproducibility columns. Input: a hypothesis produced by any generator. Output: a row carrying generator (template|local|hosted), model_id, generation_params, and raw_response, all populated on write. Constraints: these columns exist from the first migration, not a later one; model_id is a dated identifier, never an alias; raw_response stores verbatim pre-parse output. Failure case: writing a hypothesis with generator set but model_id or raw_response null must be rejected at the repository boundary for the two model arms. Refs: FR-508, FR-903, NFR-602, US-R3, US-R4, ai-004, ai-005.

Repository layer. Input: a route handler needing persisted data. Output: data obtained through a repository function; the handler contains no SQL, no session construction, and no spatial logic. Constraints: enforced by a test that greps route modules for SQL and ORM query constructs. Failure case: a raw SELECT or a PostGIS function call inside a route handler fails the spec. Refs: FR-904, US-E2, db-004.

PostGIS spatial query, the justification for the spatial database. Input: an RF anomaly zone geometry, a radius N in kilometres, and a time window. Output: the set of track discontinuities whose location falls within N km of the zone inside that window. Constraints: distance computed by PostGIS on geography, not by application-side arithmetic; the radius is a parameter, not a constant. Failure case: a discontinuity just outside N km must be excluded, and an empty result set must return an empty list rather than null or an error. Refs: FR-905, FR-305, anom-004, anom-005, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 9.

Database connectivity: engine, session, and configuration. Input: DATABASE_URL in the environment, in the form compose already passes to the backend and pipeline services. Output: sqlalchemy and psycopg added to pyproject.toml and locked; a single SQLAlchemy 2.x Engine created once during application startup and disposed on shutdown via the lifespan hook; a sessionmaker bound to it; and a FastAPI dependency yielding one Session per request that rolls back on exception and closes on completion. Constraints: the driver is psycopg 3, addressed as postgresql+psycopg://; the URL is read from the environment only, with no DSN, host, or credential literal in application source or in a fixture (NFR-401); exactly one Engine exists per process, so the connection pool is shared rather than rebuilt per request; engine construction is lazy and opens no connection, so unit tests need no live database and the live connectivity check stays in scripts/smoke-test.sh; GET /api/v1/health continues to answer without acquiring a connection, preserving api-001 so a degraded database cannot present as an unreachable service. Failure case: a missing or empty DATABASE_URL must fail loudly at startup rather than at first query; constructing an Engine inside a request handler fails the spec; and a request whose handler raises must leave no session open and no transaction uncommitted. Refs: FR-901, FR-904, NFR-401, api-001, db-001, db-003, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 10, docs/qa.md section 18.

Canonical observation model and required-field validation. Input: a source-specific record emitted by any adapter. Output: a canonical observation with source_id, source_type, observation_type, timestamp, location, data_mode, validation_status, provenance, and a typed payload. Constraints: one model for every source; payload typing is per observation type via Pydantic; validation runs before persistence. Failure case: a record missing timestamp or location must not produce a canonical observation and must route to quarantine per dal-002. Refs: FR-101, FR-102, US-E2, dal-002, dal-003.

Quarantine of malformed records. Input: a batch of records where some fail required-field validation. Output: valid records persisted as canonical observations; invalid records persisted to quarantine with the failing field, the reason, and the source attribution; a per-run count of each. Constraints: nothing is silently dropped; no invalid record aborts the ingest run; persistence happens through a repository port -- an interface accepting canonical observations and quarantine records, with the storage engine behind it -- so this item is provable against an in-memory implementation and the PostGIS implementation lands with db-001, db-003 requiring that seam regardless of build order; the two writes are one unit of work, so a run that persists observations and then fails before writing quarantine records must leave neither. What this item proves is DAL behaviour, not database enforcement: the NOT NULL and foreign-key guarantees over the same fields are db-001's to prove, and passes: true here asserts the first claim only. Failure case: a batch of ten records with three invalid must persist seven observations and three quarantine rows and complete without raising; raising, or persisting seven with no quarantine trace, fails the spec. A second failure case: a port signature carrying a storage-engine type -- a WKT or WKB string, a session, an ORM model, a database-assigned identifier the caller is expected to supply -- fails the spec, because the DAL would then know about PostGIS and the seam db-003 exists to enforce would already be broken. Refs: FR-103, NFR-102, US-E3, AC-02, dal-001, dal-003, db-001, db-003, docs/qa.md section 26.

Provenance on every accepted record. Input: a validated record and its ingest context. Output: a canonical observation carrying source ID, source type, data mode, and scenario run ID. Constraints: provenance is attached at the DAL, not per adapter, so it cannot be forgotten by a new adapter; data_mode distinguishes replayed from synthetic. The guarantee is asserted twice, at different layers and at different times: the DAL must refuse to construct a record with provenance missing, which is what this item proves, and the schema must refuse to store one, which is db-001's NOT NULL constraints and is proven there. Marking this item passing therefore asserts the DAL half only, and the constraint half is outstanding until db-001 lands. Failure case: a canonical observation constructed with a null scenario run ID or an absent data mode fails the spec. A second failure case: provenance applied inside an adapter rather than at the DAL passes its own tests while leaving the next adapter free to omit it, which is the failure this item exists to prevent and is asserted by driving two different adapters through the same DAL entrypoint. Refs: FR-104, US-A7, US-E2, AC-02, dal-001, dal-002, db-001, adp-003, docs/qa.md section 26.

Aircraft identifier pseudonymisation at the DAL. Input: a validated source record carrying source-native aircraft identifiers (icao24 and callsign for the OpenSky adapter) and a pseudonymisation seed held as fixed project configuration and recorded in the corpus manifest. Output: a canonical observation in which those identifiers are replaced by deterministic pseudonyms, with the source values discarded rather than retained alongside. Constraints: the substitution happens at the DAL, not per adapter, so a new adapter cannot forget it -- the same argument dal-003 makes for provenance; the pseudonym is a deterministic function of the source identifier and the configured seed, so one aircraft maps to one pseudonym within and across runs and track continuity survives for the detectors; no reverse mapping is persisted anywhere the application can read, so a pseudonym cannot be resolved back from the database or an API response; the pseudonym carries no source information, so airline prefixes and country blocks encoded in a callsign or an icao24 allocation do not survive into it; the real identifiers remain in the local extract, which the licence permits, since the restriction is on publication and disclosure rather than on local use. The seed is separate from the scenario seed and is never drawn per run: the mapping is a property of the corpus, not of a run, because the extract is a single replayed hour and the same airframes recur in every run of a batch. One aircraft therefore carries one pseudonym across every run, and scn-001's byte-identical guarantee for a given type, parameters and seed is unaffected, since nothing about the mapping varies with those three values. Changing the seed is a corpus-level event, recorded in the manifest alongside the extract checksum, not a per-run parameter. Failure case: a real icao24 or callsign appearing in an API response, an evidence bundle, a hypothesis, a hosted-provider request payload, or a rendered screen fails the spec, because OpenSky Data License Agreement section 3(i) requires aircraft identifiers to be de-identified for any publication or other disclosure and section 3(iii) forbids making the data available outside the licensee's institute. A second failure case: the same aircraft carrying different pseudonyms in two runs against the same corpus, which breaks track continuity across a replay and makes a batch non-comparable; deriving the pseudonym from the scenario seed produces exactly this and fails the spec. A third failure case: retaining the source identifier in the observation payload beside the pseudonym, which satisfies the letter of the mapping while leaving the real value one query away. Refs: FR-111, NFR-405, FR-101, FR-104, US-E2, AC-02, dal-001, dal-003, adp-001, adp-003, adp-004, evb-001, ai-004, docs/qa.md section 22.

OpenSky replay adapter. Input: the archived, bounding-box-filtered OpenSky extract, stored as a committed Parquet file with its manifest, and a replay position in simulated time. Output: source records carrying lat, lon, baroaltitude or geoaltitude, velocity, heading, lastposupdate, and lastcontact, converted by the DAL into canonical track observations. Constraints: reads from file only, never the network, so replays are deterministic, offline, and reproducible from a fresh clone with no download step; position staleness is the measured delta between time and lastposupdate, not an inferred value; Parquet is the archive format for this extract alone and is never a read path for observations, which are served from PostGIS. Failure case: a row with a null lat or lon must quarantine rather than persist a track observation at a default coordinate. A second failure case: an adapter that falls back to fetching from the OpenSky API when the extract is missing, which silently reintroduces the network dependency the archive exists to remove. Refs: FR-105, FR-110, NFR-101, dal-001, dal-002, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5 data sources.

Synthetic RF adapter. Input: scenario type, parameters, and seed from the scenario generator. Output: RF source records on a sensor x channel x time grid, each carrying sensor ID, sensor location, timestamp, channel index, channel centre frequency, band, power, SNR, bandwidth, signal type, and baseline delta, converted by the DAL into canonical RF observations. Constraints: fully determined by scenario type, parameters, and seed; emits no data of its own accord outside a scenario run; every sensor reports on every channel at every interval, so a missing reading is a detectable gap rather than an ambiguous absence; carries no ground-truth field, per api-009. Failure case: two runs with identical type, parameters, and seed producing different RF observation sequences fails the spec. A second failure case: emitting a sparse grid in which a sensor silently omits channels it has nothing to report on, which makes a genuine dropout indistinguishable from a design choice. Refs: FR-106, FR-108, FR-201, scn-001, scn-005, api-009, dal-001, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5 data sources.

Third source adapter, the extensibility measurement. Input: a simple additional source, for example a synthetic source-health feed. Output: canonical observations of a new observation type flowing through the unchanged DAL, plus a recorded measurement of files touched, lines changed, and hours taken. Constraints: the DAL, canonical model, and detection layer must require no modification beyond registering the adapter and its payload type; this is RQ1 evidence, not a feature, and is built late. Failure case: needing to alter the canonical observation model or a detection rule to accommodate the new source is a reportable negative result and fails the spec as written. Refs: FR-107, US-E2, US-R6, dal-001, docs/research_scope.md RQ1.

OpenSky corpus extraction and archive. Input: a locally downloaded raw OpenSky hourly state-vector file (states_YYYY-MM-DD-HH.csv.tar, wrapping one gzipped CSV member, from the anonymously readable data-samples bucket), a bounding box, and an output directory. Output: under data/opensky/ -- opensky_extract.parquet, the bounding-box-filtered Parquet extract, gitignored and never committed, plus a bounded sample of rows whose lat or lon is null, retained deliberately so the quarantine path has real input; manifest.json, committed, recording source URL, snapshot hour, download date, the licence and the required attribution text verbatim, the SHA-256 checksum of the original raw file, and a content checksum of the extract; and coverage.json, committed, the coverage report giving the per-icao24 inter-sample gap distribution against the 10-second cadence. Constraints: neither the raw file nor the extract may be committed, because the OpenSky Data License Agreement section 3(iii) forbids making the data available to anyone outside the licensee's institute; reproducibility is carried instead by the committed manifest plus a fetch-and-filter entrypoint that re-downloads against the recorded checksum and re-filters, so a fresh clone reproduces the extract in one command once the reader accepts the same licence; download and filter are separate operations and the filter itself performs no network access, so it is testable offline against a small fixture; filtering is deterministic, so re-running against the same raw file and bounding box yields an extract with identical row content and column schema, verified against the recorded content checksum rather than by byte equality, since Parquet writers embed non-deterministic metadata; licence and attribution are captured at download time and stored verbatim, because the terms as published on that date cannot be reconstructed later; Parquet is the archive format for this extract alone and is never a read path for observations, which are served from PostGIS; the corpus lives under data/opensky/ rather than scenarios/, which is reserved for scenario fixtures -- this is replayed source data, not a fixture. A bounding-box test cannot be applied to a null coordinate, so a pure spatial filter would exclude every null-position row and leave dal-002's quarantine path exercised by fixtures alone and AC-02 undemonstrated on real data; the filter therefore also retains the first N rows with a null lat or lon in file order, N being configuration with its value and the resulting count recorded in the manifest. File order is used rather than a seeded sample so the retention needs no seed of its own and stays deterministic for a given raw file. Such a row can only ever reach quarantine, never a canonical observation, so retaining it adds evidence without any risk of contaminating the operational picture or a metric. The coverage report computes its gap distribution over positioned rows only, since a null-position row is not a coverage gap. Failure case: a filter step that downloads the snapshot itself when the raw file is absent fails the spec, because it reintroduces the network dependency the archive exists to remove and makes the filter untestable offline -- the same failure adp-001 guards against at replay time. A second failure case: opensky_extract.parquet or the raw file appearing in git fails the spec as a licence breach, and a manifest missing the original checksum, the licence, or the attribution text fails it because the artefact is then neither reproducible nor attributable. A third failure case: an extract containing no null-position rows at all, which silently removes the only real-data input dal-002 has and reduces AC-02 to a fixture claim. A fourth failure case: a coverage report whose natural gap distribution overlaps the gap durations the aircraft-coverage-gap scenario will inject must fail acceptance and force a different bounding box, never be waived, because genuine and injected dropouts would then be indistinguishable and the false-positive rate uninterpretable. Refs: FR-105, FR-110, NFR-101, NFR-105, NFR-601, AC-02, adp-001, scn-002, anom-008, docs/implementation.md Track 0, docs/qa.md section 21.

Fetch-and-verify entrypoint for the OpenSky corpus, the network half of the corpus tooling. Input: a source URL and expected SHA-256 read from the committed manifest, a destination directory, and an explicit licence acceptance. Output: the raw tarball downloaded to data/opensky/raw/ and verified against the recorded checksum, followed by the adp-004 filter, so one command takes a fresh clone to opensky_extract.parquet, manifest.json and coverage.json. Constraints: this is the only module in the corpus tooling permitted to open a socket, which is what keeps the adp-004 filter network-free and testable offline; the checksum of the downloaded file is verified before the filter runs, not after, so a corrupted or substituted file never reaches the extract; the download writes to a temporary path and is moved into place only once verified, so an interrupted run leaves nothing that a later run would mistake for a complete file; a run whose destination already holds a file matching the recorded checksum skips the download rather than re-fetching roughly 180 MB; licence acceptance is an explicit act by the operator, not a default, and the licence and attribution are displayed at the point of acceptance, because the whole reason the extract is not committed is that acceptance belongs to the reader rather than being bypassed by handing them the bytes; every test mocks the transport and no test in the suite performs a real download. Failure case: a checksum mismatch that still produces an extract fails the spec, because the artefact would then be unattributable to the recorded source and the manifest would assert a provenance that does not hold; the run must abort and leave no extract, manifest or coverage report behind. A second failure case: a partially downloaded file left at the destination path, which a later run would accept as complete and filter into a silently truncated extract. A third failure case: downloading without explicit licence acceptance, which makes the tool take a licence action on the operator's behalf. A fourth failure case: any test performing a real network call, which makes the suite slow, non-deterministic, dependent on OpenSky's hosting, and quietly turns continuous integration into an unattended acceptor of someone else's terms. Refs: FR-110, NFR-101, NFR-105, NFR-601, AC-12, adp-001, adp-004, ops-003, docs/qa.md section 21, docs/implementation.md Track 0.

Seeded reproducibility of scenario runs. Input: a scenario type, a parameter set, and an integer seed. Output: a run whose emitted observation sequence is byte-identical to any other run with the same three values. Constraints: no wall-clock time, no unseeded randomness, and no process-dependent ordering may influence output; the seed used is always recorded, including when generated. Failure case: identical inputs producing different output, or differing seeds producing identical output, both fail the spec. Refs: FR-201, US-E1, NFR-601, AC-01, api-006, scn-003.

The five scenario types. Input: one of normal-baseline, gnss-degradation, rf-sensor-fault, aircraft-coverage-gap, ambiguous-mixed-evidence, with parameters and seed. Output: an observation stream exhibiting that scenario's signature, plus a ground-truth record stating what was injected, where, in which channels, and in which simulated window. Constraints: exactly five types in v1; spectral extent is a parameter of gnss-degradation, narrowband confined to the L1 channel or broadband across the grid, not a sixth scenario type; ground truth is recorded at generation time, never inferred afterwards from detector output. Failure case: normal-baseline injecting any deviation at all fails the spec, because anom-008 and the false-positive rate depend on it being genuinely clean. A second failure case: adding a sixth scenario type for broadband interference rather than parameterising the existing one. Refs: FR-202, FR-204, FR-108, anom-008, scn-005, AC-04, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.2.

Batch execution. Input: a scenario type, a parameter distribution, a base seed, and a run count between 20 and 30. Output: N runs with distinct derived seeds, each with its own recorded parameters and ground truth, executed without manual intervention. Constraints: derived seeds are a deterministic function of the base seed, so the whole batch is reproducible from one value; a failing run is recorded and skipped rather than aborting the batch. Failure case: one run raising and terminating the batch, or two runs in a batch sharing a seed, fails the spec. Refs: FR-205, FR-1001, US-R2, scn-001, eval-001.

Scenario Control screen. Input: the five scenario types and the recent-runs list from GET /api/v1/scenario/runs. Output: a scenario library, a run configuration form for parameters, seed, and batch count, run controls for start, pause, reset, and replay, a run status indicator, and a recent-runs table showing type, seed, and outcome. Constraints: the seed field is visible and editable, because this screen is the visible face of the evaluation harness; replay of a listed run reuses its exact recorded seed and parameters. Failure case: starting a run with no seed entered and no seed shown afterwards fails the spec, since the run would be unreproducible. Refs: FR-714, FR-201, US-E1, api-006, scn-001, nav-001.

RF sensor and channel layout. Input: the scenario configuration. Output: a fixed grid of six to eight RF sensors at recorded geographic positions, each reporting on eight 2 MHz channels with centre frequencies 1567.42, 1569.42, 1571.42, 1573.42, 1575.42, 1577.42, 1579.42 and 1581.42 MHz, at a fixed interval of simulated time. Constraints: one channel is centred exactly on GNSS L1 at 1575.42 MHz with four channels either side, so frequency adjacency runs in both directions; sensor positions are chosen so that a candidate interference zone contains some sensors and excludes others, which is what makes the spatial-coherence test in anom-005 and the neighbour test in anom-007 discriminating rather than vacuous; the layout is configuration, not hard-coded constants, so it can be varied without editing detector code. Failure case: a layout with fewer than four sensors, or one in which every sensor falls inside every plausible affected area, makes spatial clustering undiscriminating and fails the spec. A second failure case: a channel plan with no channel centred on L1, which removes the band the gnss-degradation scenario targets. Refs: FR-108, FR-109, scn-002, adp-002, anom-002, anom-004, anom-005, anom-007, evb-001, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5 data sources.

RF threshold rule, rule ID RF-NOISE. Input: RF observations in a window and the baseline for the band from anom-002. Output: an anomaly of type rf_noise_deviation carrying severity, time window, affected area, and the observation IDs that triggered it. Constraints: the threshold is configuration, not a literal in the rule; the rule is deterministic, so the same observations always give the same anomaly. Failure case: observations at exactly the baseline must produce no anomaly, and observations one unit above threshold must produce exactly one. Refs: FR-301, FR-303, anom-002, evb-001, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.3.

Rolling-average baseline engine. Input: observations from normal-baseline runs, a metric, and a window length. Output: a baseline value against which deviation is measured, computed per metric per sensor per channel for RF metrics and per metric per region for track metrics. Constraints: the baseline derives from normal-scenario data only; per-channel granularity is required so that a quiet channel and a noisy one on the same sensor are not averaged into a baseline that fits neither; a window with insufficient samples returns an explicit insufficient-data result, not a misleading average over one point. Failure case: computing a baseline from a window containing injected anomaly data, or returning a value from a single sample as if it were a baseline, fails the spec. A second failure case: pooling channels into one per-sensor baseline, which hides single-channel deviations inside the spread of the others. Refs: FR-302, FR-301, FR-108, anom-001, anom-003, anom-007, scn-002, scn-005.

Z-score deviation detector. Input: a metric series, its baseline mean and standard deviation from anom-002, and a z threshold. Output: anomalies for points whose absolute z-score exceeds the threshold, each carrying the computed z and the rule ID. Constraints: the z value is stored on the anomaly for traceability but is never rendered to the analyst as a score, per ui-001. Failure case: a series with zero standard deviation must not divide by zero; it returns no anomalies and records the degenerate baseline. Refs: FR-301, ui-001, anom-002, evb-002.

Spatial clustering of track discontinuities. Input: track-continuity anomalies in a time window and a cluster radius. Output: clusters of discontinuities with a representative centroid and affected-area geometry, computed by the PostGIS query in db-004. Constraints: clustering is spatial and deterministic; isolated discontinuities outside the radius form no cluster. Failure case: two discontinuities separated by more than the radius must not be reported as one cluster. Refs: FR-301, FR-305, db-004, anom-005.

Fusion rule, rule ID FUSION-SPATIAL. Input: RF noise anomalies from anom-001 and track-gap clusters from anom-004. Output: an anomaly of type possible_interference_zone when both occur in the same simulated time window and within the configured distance, carrying references to both contributing anomalies. Constraints: both conditions are necessary; the window and distance are configuration. Failure case: RF noise and track gaps in the same area but in non-overlapping time windows must not raise this anomaly, and neither must a co-occurrence with only one of the two present. Refs: FR-305, US-A2, db-004, anom-001, anom-004, evb-001.

Data-source issue rule, rule ID SOURCE-GAP. Input: track dropout clusters and the set of RF anomalies for the same window and area. Output: an anomaly of type possible_data_source_issue when dropouts are present and no co-located RF anomaly exists. Constraints: this rule is the discriminator that keeps a coverage gap from being reported as interference; it is mutually exclusive with anom-005 for the same cluster. Failure case: an aircraft-coverage-gap scenario producing possible_interference_zone instead of possible_data_source_issue fails the spec. Refs: FR-306, scn-002, anom-005, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.3.

Sensor fault rule, rule ID SENSOR-FAULT. Input: an RF sensor reporting abnormal readings, the readings of its spatial neighbours in the same window, and the readings of the frequency-adjacent channels on the sensor itself. Output: an anomaly of type possible_sensor_fault when the sensor is abnormal and its spatial neighbours are nominal, with the frequency-adjacency test recorded as a distinct piece of evidence rather than folded into the spatial one. Constraints: spatial neighbour selection is a spatial query with a configured radius, not a hard-coded sensor list; frequency neighbour selection is the adjacent channel indices on the same sensor. A real emission raises adjacent channels together, so an isolated single-channel deviation with clean neighbours is evidence about the sensor rather than the environment. Failure case: several adjacent sensors all reporting abnormal readings must not raise a sensor-fault anomaly, since that pattern indicates an environmental cause. A second failure case: a deviation spanning all eight channels on one sensor being reported with the same confidence as a single-channel one, since the broadband pattern is weaker evidence of a fault. Refs: FR-307, FR-108, scn-002, scn-005, db-004, anom-001, anom-002.

Correct non-detection on a normal-baseline run. Input: a completed normal-baseline scenario run with no injected deviation. Output: zero anomalies of any type. Constraints: this is a required positive behaviour of the detection engine, not an absence of behaviour; it is asserted for every detector, not only in aggregate. Failure case: any anomaly raised on a clean run fails the spec, because the false-positive rate reported in eval-002 becomes meaningless if the engine is noisy on clean data. Refs: FR-308, US-R5, AC-04, scn-002, eval-002, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 14.

Detection latency measurement. Input: an anomaly and its scenario run ground truth. Output: latency as the simulated-time delta between injected event onset and anomaly emission. Constraints: simulated scenario time only, never wall clock; the definition is fixed before any measurement code exists, per the Track 0 item in docs/implementation.md; the unit is recorded alongside the value. Failure case: a latency that changes when the same run is replayed on faster hardware fails the spec, because it proves wall-clock time leaked in. Refs: FR-309, FR-1002, NFR-601, scn-001, eval-002.

Evidence bundle builder. Input: a group of related anomalies from one scenario run, grouped on three axes: simulated time window, spatial proximity, and frequency adjacency. Output: a bundle containing anomaly_type, time_window, affected_area, affected_channels, data_mode, an evidence list where each item has source, finding, and rule_id, and a known_uncertainties list. Constraints: this bundle is the only input the AI layer ever receives; raw observations never reach a model; anomalies on adjacent channels of the same sensor within the same window group into one bundle rather than several; the bundle carries no ground-truth field, per api-009. Failure case: an evidence item lacking a rule_id, or a bundle built with an empty evidence list, fails the spec. A second failure case: a broadband event spanning eight channels producing eight single-channel bundles, which fragments one finding into eight and hands the AI layer an incoherent picture. Refs: FR-401, FR-402, FR-404, FR-108, US-R1, AC-05, ai-003, api-009, scn-005, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.4.

Evidence traceability. Input: a candidate evidence bundle. Output: a built bundle in which every evidence item resolves to a stored anomaly or observation ID. Constraints: resolution is checked at build time against the database, not asserted by the builder; the resolved IDs are persisted with the bundle so the grounding check in ai-008 has something to verify against. Failure case: a bundle containing an item whose rule_id or source reference matches no stored record must raise and must not persist a partial bundle. Refs: FR-403, US-R1, AC-05, evb-001, ai-008.

Hypothesis output schema. Input: a candidate hypothesis object from any generator. Output: a validated Pydantic model with hypothesis_title, confidence, summary, supporting_evidence, evidence_against_or_uncertainty, alternative_explanations, and recommended_human_action. Constraints: confidence is an enum of exactly Low, Medium, High; all fields are required; the same schema serves all three generators and is the source from which the hosted JSON schema and the local grammar are derived. Failure case: a hypothesis with confidence 87% or 0.87 must be unrepresentable, and one with a missing alternative_explanations field must fail validation rather than defaulting to empty. Refs: FR-501, FR-715, NFR-203, ui-001, ai-002, ai-004, ai-005.

Template hypothesis generator. Input: an evidence bundle. Output: a schema-valid hypothesis assembled deterministically from the bundle contents, with no model call. Constraints: no network, no API key, no model server; it is both the correctness fallback for ai-007 and the comparison baseline for the evaluation, so it must be usable in both roles; every supporting-evidence item it emits is copied from the bundle and is therefore grounded by construction. Failure case: the template generator emitting a claim absent from the bundle fails the spec and would invalidate the baseline. Refs: FR-502, US-R1, ai-001, ai-007, eval-004, docs/implementation.md Phase 9.

Provider-agnostic hypothesis service interface. Input: an evidence bundle plus configuration naming the provider, model ID, and generation parameters. Output: a validated hypothesis. Constraints: the interface is defined before either model provider is written, so no provider's request or response shape leaks into it; adding a provider touches one adapter module and configuration, nothing else; this doubles as a second data point for the RQ1 extensibility claim. Failure case: a provider-specific type appearing in the interface signature, or a caller having to branch on provider, fails the spec. Refs: FR-503, US-E2, US-R6, ai-004, ai-005, adp-003, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 10.

Hosted AI generator, the primary arm. Input: an evidence bundle, a pinned dated model ID, and frozen generation parameters. Output: a validated hypothesis persisted with generator=hosted, model_id, generation_params, and verbatim raw_response. Constraints: uses the provider's native JSON-schema-constrained output so schema conformance is a generation-time guarantee; the model ID is dated, never a moving alias; tests mock the provider and never make a real call. Failure case: a configuration naming a moving alias rather than a dated ID must be rejected at startup, since an alias changing mid-campaign would invalidate the comparison with no visible error. Refs: FR-504, FR-506, FR-507, FR-508, US-R3, US-R4, db-002, ai-001, ai-003.

Local AI generator, the second arm and availability fallback. Input: an evidence bundle and the same frozen generation parameters as ai-004. Output: a validated hypothesis persisted with generator=local, model_id, generation_params, and raw_response. Constraints: schema enforced by a grammar compiled from the same JSON Schema as ai-004, so one schema has two enforcement mechanisms and an identical guarantee; the model server runs on the host and is reached over HTTP as a config value, never as a Compose service. Failure case: the local and hosted arms diverging in accepted schema, or generation parameters differing between arms, fails the spec and would make the comparison meaningless. Refs: FR-505, FR-506, FR-1102, ai-001, ai-003, ai-004, ai-006.

Availability fallback, hosted to local. Input: a generation request while the hosted provider is unreachable, unauthenticated, or rate limited. Output: a hypothesis generated by the local arm, persisted with generator=local, and the fallback event logged. Constraints: no error state reaches the analyst; the fallback is a distinct code path from the correctness fallback in ai-007 and must remain distinct in code and in the write-up; it is deliberately exercised with the network off, not assumed. Failure case: a hosted timeout surfacing as an error in the UI, or falling through to the template generator instead of the local arm, fails the spec. Refs: FR-509, FR-511, NFR-103, NFR-105, AC-07, ai-005, ai-007, ai-010.

Correctness fallback, model arm to template. Input: a model response that fails Pydantic validation or the grounding check in ai-008. Output: a bounded number of retries, then a template-generated hypothesis persisted with generator=template and the fallback reason logged. Constraints: the retry ceiling is explicit with no unbounded recursion, because a retry loop is the realistic route to an unexpected bill; retry rate is logged per arm; this path applies identically to the hosted and local arms. Failure case: unbounded retry on persistently invalid output, or falling back to template without recording that a fallback occurred, fails the spec. Refs: FR-510, FR-511, NFR-103, ai-002, ai-006, ai-008, ai-009.

Automated grounding check. Input: a schema-valid hypothesis and the evidence bundle it was generated from. Output: a per-item grounded or ungrounded determination, a grounding_passed flag on the hypothesis, and a logged catch rate per generator arm. Constraints: this is the load-bearing safeguard, because constrained decoding guarantees shape but says nothing about whether the rule IDs inside the items exist in the bundle; the catch rate is a reportable evaluation result, not merely a safety net. Failure case: a hypothesis citing rule ID RF-NOISE-999, which is absent from the bundle, must be caught and flagged or rejected rather than passing on the basis of well-formed structure. Refs: FR-512, NFR-202, US-R1, AC-06, evb-002, ai-007, eval-005, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.5.

Run-level call budget. Input: a configured maximum number of model calls or maximum spend for a run. Output: the run aborts with a clear reason when the budget is exceeded, and the calls made so far are recorded. Constraints: this is in-code and independent of the provider-console hard cap, which is the backstop; per-call token and cost logging is in place from the very first call, not retrofitted. Failure case: a retry loop exhausting the budget without aborting, or aborting without recording what was already spent, fails the spec. Refs: FR-513, FR-514, ai-007, eval-005.

Generator provenance surfaced in the UI. Input: a hypothesis carrying its generator field. Output: a visible indicator on the hypothesis card and detail view naming the producing generator. Constraints: a hypothesis produced by either fallback path is visibly distinguishable from a primary-arm one; degradation is shown, never hidden. Failure case: a template-fallback hypothesis rendering identically to a hosted-arm one fails the spec, because the analyst would not know the AI layer had degraded. Refs: FR-713, NFR-204, US-A8, ai-006, ai-007, hyp-001, api-004.

Hypothesis Detail header. Input: a hypothesis from GET /api/v1/hypotheses/{id}. Output: title, status, confidence pips, affected area, and time window rendered in the detail header, with a zone map thumbnail and a mini timeline. Constraints: confidence renders through the ui-001 primitive; status is one of New, Under review, Confirmed, Rejected, Inconclusive; the map thumbnail goes through the MapView boundary. Failure case: an unknown hypothesis ID rendering an empty header rather than an explicit not-found state fails the spec. Refs: FR-711, FR-715, ui-001, map-001, api-004, nav-001.

Supporting evidence with traceability markers. Input: a hypothesis supporting_evidence list and its grounding results from ai-008. Output: one row per evidence item showing source, finding, a rule-ID chip, and a grounded marker. Constraints: grounded state is exposed non-visually so tests assert on it rather than on styling; an ungrounded item is displayed and marked as ungrounded, never silently removed. Failure case: hiding an ungrounded evidence item fails the spec, because concealing it removes the analyst's ability to judge the failure. Refs: FR-711, NFR-202, NFR-204, US-A4, ai-008, hyp-001.

Uncertainty and alternative explanations. Input: a hypothesis evidence_against_or_uncertainty and alternative_explanations fields. Output: both sections rendered on Hypothesis Detail, adjacent to supporting evidence rather than behind a disclosure. Constraints: both are always rendered; an empty list renders an explicit none recorded state so absence is visible rather than ambiguous. Failure case: collapsing alternatives behind a hidden accordion, or omitting the section when empty, fails the spec, since the point is to prevent anchoring on one interpretation. Refs: FR-711, NFR-201, US-A5, ai-001, hyp-001.

Decision-support disclaimer. Input: none. Output: the text Decision support only, analyst judgement is final, rendered on Hypothesis Detail. Constraints: always present, not conditional and not dismissible; consistent with the framing in the README and on every screen. Failure case: the disclaimer absent from the rendered detail view, or present only in a tooltip, fails the spec. Refs: FR-712, NFR-303, NFR-304, hyp-001.

Analyst verdict submission. Input: an analyst activating confirm, reject, needs more evidence, or false positive on Hypothesis Detail. Output: a POST to /api/v1/hypotheses/{id}/feedback, a persisted feedback row, an updated hypothesis status, and the new status reflected in the UI. Constraints: exactly four verdicts; the change survives a reload, because a verdict that is not persisted is not human-in-the-loop validation; status transition follows the documented state set. Failure case: a failed POST leaving the UI showing the new status while the database still holds the old one fails the spec. Refs: FR-601, FR-602, US-A6, AC-09, api-005, hyp-001.

Analyst note and verdict validation. Input: a verdict with an optional free-text note. Output: the note persisted alongside the verdict and shown in the hypothesis feedback history. Constraints: the note is optional and never required to submit a verdict; input is validated at the API boundary. Failure case: an unrecognised verdict value must be rejected with 422, must persist no feedback row, and must leave hypothesis status unchanged. Refs: FR-603, FR-604, NFR-402, api-005, fbk-001.

Batch runner. Input: a scenario type, parameter distribution, base seed, and run count between 20 and 30. Output: N completed runs per type, each with recorded parameters, seed, ground truth, and detector output, executed unattended. Constraints: the entire batch is reproducible from the base seed; a single failing run is recorded and skipped rather than aborting the batch. Failure case: a batch that cannot be reproduced from its recorded base seed fails the spec, since every downstream metric would then be unverifiable. Refs: FR-1001, FR-205, US-R2, scn-001, scn-003.

Detection metrics. Input: batch run outputs and their recorded ground truth. Output: precision, recall, F1, false positive rate, false negative rate, and detection latency per scenario type. Constraints: latency is in simulated time per anom-009; normal-baseline runs contribute to the false positive rate, which is why anom-008 must hold; metric definitions are documented alongside the numbers. Failure case: a batch with zero true positives must produce a documented undefined or zero precision rather than dividing by zero. Refs: FR-1002, US-R2, US-R5, AC-10, anom-008, anom-009.

Metrics export. Input: computed metrics from eval-002 and eval-005. Output: CSV and JSON files suitable for direct use in thesis tables and charts, including the run parameters and seeds that produced them. Constraints: exports are self-describing, so a table in the write-up can be traced back to the exact runs behind it. Failure case: an export omitting the seeds and parameters fails the spec, because the numbers would then be unreproducible. Refs: FR-1003, NFR-601, AC-10, eval-001, eval-002.

Anonymised two-arm hypothesis export for blind scoring. Input: a stratified sample of evidence bundles (approximately 5 per anomalous scenario type, ~20 total) processed by the hosted and template generators, one scored generation per arm per bundle. Output: a scoring pack containing the rendered hypothesis pairs in randomised within-bundle order with identical formatting across arms, the arm key written to a separate file, and a blank score sheet per rater carrying the dimensions defined in docs/scoring_rubric.md. Constraints: the arm is not inferable from the exported text, including from formatting artefacts, field ordering, or whitespace; the corpus and the rubric are fixed before the campaign runs, not adjusted after seeing results; the local arm is excluded from scoring and its exclusion is recorded rather than silent. Failure case: an export in which the template arm is identifiable by its phrasing or layout invalidates the blind comparison and fails the spec. Refs: FR-1004, US-R3, ai-002, ai-004, eval-006, docs/scoring_rubric.md, docs/em_fusion_v2.md section 5.9.

Per-arm AI statistics. Input: all hypothesis generations from a campaign, across every generator that ran. Output: grounding catch rate, grounding variance across N generations per bundle, retry rate, actual cost, and wall-time, each broken down by generator arm. Constraints: recorded per arm rather than in aggregate, because the comparison between arms is the result; computed over all N generations, which is a separate and larger population than the one-generation-per-arm corpus that eval-004 exports for human scoring; the local arm is reported here when it ran as a fallback even though it is not blind-scored, since fallback frequency is itself a reliability result; cost and wall-time are write-up material and make the deliberate-spend claim concrete. Failure case: reporting a single pooled grounding catch rate across arms fails the spec, since it hides the very difference being measured. Refs: FR-1005, US-R3, ai-008, ai-009, eval-003, eval-004.

Blind-score ingest and inter-rater agreement. Input: completed score sheets from two independent raters over the eval-004 scoring pack, plus the separately held arm key. Output: per-dimension mean and distribution per arm, the hosted-versus-template difference per dimension, and quadratic-weighted Cohen's kappa computed across the whole double-scored corpus. Constraints: the arm key is joined only after both sheets are ingested, so scores cannot be attributed to an arm during entry; every scored item carries two independent scores, so agreement is reported over the full corpus rather than a subset; the pre-registered adjudication rule is applied to disagreements rather than chosen after inspecting them; a rater who scored only part of the corpus is reported as partial coverage rather than silently averaged. Failure case: computing kappa over items scored by one rater only, or silently substituting a single rater's score where the second is missing, overstates agreement and fails the spec. Refs: FR-1004, FR-1006, US-R3, eval-003, eval-004, docs/scoring_rubric.md.

Docker Compose full stack. Input: docker compose up on a clean machine with Docker installed. Output: frontend, backend, and PostgreSQL with PostGIS running and reachable, with migrations applied and the app usable end to end. Constraints: no cloud account and no external service required; the local model server is a host process referenced by config through host.docker.internal, never a Compose service, because Docker Desktop on macOS does not pass Metal through. Failure case: a Compose file declaring the model server as a service fails the spec, and a first-run start that requires an undocumented manual step fails AC-12. Refs: FR-1101, FR-1102, NFR-105, AC-12, ai-005.

CI pipeline. Input: a pushed commit or opened pull request. Output: backend pytest, frontend vitest and build, lint on both halves, and a basic dependency audit, each reported as a separate check. Constraints: no Trivy, no container scanning, no deployment step in v1; a failing test fails the pipeline rather than warning. Failure case: a commit that breaks a frontend test passing CI, or a lint failure reported only as a warning, fails the spec. Refs: FR-1103, NFR-404, US-E6, AC-12.

Root Makefile as the containerised command surface. Input: a make target run from the repo root. Output: generate runs a scenario batch in a container; demo runs generate then brings the stack up with a build; build builds all images; test runs the backend pytest suite and the frontend vitest suite in containers; up starts the stack; down tears it down with orphans removed. Constraints: every target delegates to docker compose, so the root Makefile needs no host toolchain beyond Docker; backend/Makefile is retained unchanged for local venv work and the two are not merged; this item is blocked on ops-001, since the Compose file must exist first. Failure case: a target that succeeds while the underlying compose command fails, or a test target that reports success when either suite had failures, fails the spec. Refs: FR-1104, US-E7, AC-12, ops-001, ops-002.
